exercises.prompt: ___ woon in Nederland.
exercises.explanationEn: Use ik as the subject: the person doing the action.

exercises.prompt: Sara is mijn collega. ___ werkt in Amsterdam.
exercises.explanationEn: Use zij/ze for a female subject.

exercises.prompt: Mijn broer en ik? ___ gaan met de trein.
exercises.explanationEn: Use wij/we for the subject of the sentence.

exercises.prompt: Waar is Peter? ___ is thuis.
exercises.explanationEn: Use hij as the subject for a male person.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: A time expression can come first; the finite verb stays in second position.
acceptedSentences: Morgen gaan wij naar de huisarts.

exercises.prompt: Match the subject pronoun to its English meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: Some forms have more than one meaning depending on context.

exercises.prompt: Dit is ___ fiets. Ik gebruik hem elke dag.
exercises.explanationEn: Mijn means 'my' and comes before the noun.

exercises.prompt: Fatima zoekt ___ sleutels.
exercises.explanationEn: Use haar for 'her' when the possessor is female.

exercises.prompt: Wij bezoeken ___ ouders op zondag.
exercises.explanationEn: Use onze with a plural noun; ouders is plural.

exercises.prompt: Waar is ___ paspoort, meneer?
exercises.explanationEn: Uw is the formal possessive 'your'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: The possessive comes before the noun: mijn broer.

exercises.prompt: Match the possessive to its English meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: Use ons with het-words singular and onze with de-words and plurals.

exercises.prompt: Kun je ___ helpen? (I am the person you help.)
exercises.explanationEn: After the verb, use the object form mij/me, not subject ik.

exercises.prompt: Ik zie Anna. Ik zie ___.
exercises.explanationEn: Use haar as the object pronoun referring to Anna.

exercises.prompt: De docent belt Mark. De docent belt ___.
exercises.explanationEn: Use hem as the object form for a male person.

exercises.prompt: Wil je ___ even bellen? (we)
exercises.explanationEn: Use ons as the object form of wij/we.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: A common pattern is subject + verb + indirect object + direct object; time placement can vary.
acceptedSentences: Ik geef haar morgen het boek.

exercises.prompt: Match the subject form to its object form.
exercises.explanationEn: Dutch often uses short forms such as me, je and ze in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Elke dag ___ ik om zeven uur. (werken)
exercises.explanationEn: With ik, use the verb stem: werken → werk.

exercises.prompt: Mijn zus ___ in een ziekenhuis. (werken)
exercises.explanationEn: With hij/zij/het, add -t to the stem: werk → werkt.

exercises.prompt: Gisteren ___ we thuis. (werken)
exercises.explanationEn: For plural subjects in the simple past, use -ten/-den; werken → werkten.

exercises.prompt: Ik heb gisteren veel ___. (werken)
exercises.explanationEn: Perfectum: hebben + past participle; werken → gewerkt.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: The finite verb usually comes second in a main clause.
acceptedSentences: De winkel opent om negen uur.

exercises.prompt: Match each infinitive to its past participle.
exercises.explanationEn: Many regular past participles use ge- + stem + t/d; spelling follows Dutch rules.

exercises.prompt: Wij ___ een afspraak bij de huisarts.
exercises.explanationEn: Use hebben to say 'we have' an appointment.

exercises.prompt: Ik ___ moe na het werk.
exercises.explanationEn: Use zijn for a state: ik ben moe.

exercises.prompt: Gisteren ___ zij naar huis gegaan.
exercises.explanationEn: Many verbs of movement/change use zijn in the perfectum: zij is gegaan.

exercises.prompt: We ___ de boodschappen gedaan.
exercises.explanationEn: Use hebben with doen in this perfectum sentence.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: In the perfectum, the auxiliary is finite and the participle usually goes to the end.
acceptedSentences: Ik ben om acht uur vertrokken.

exercises.prompt: Match the infinitive to the auxiliary commonly used in the perfectum.
exercises.explanationEn: These are common patterns for A2; auxiliary choice can depend on the verb's use and meaning.

exercises.prompt: Ik ___ morgen werken. (must / have to)
exercises.explanationEn: Moeten expresses obligation: ik moet.

exercises.prompt: ___ je mij helpen, alsjeblieft? (can)
exercises.explanationEn: Kun je...? asks whether someone is able to help.

exercises.prompt: Je ___ hier niet roken. (not allowed)
exercises.explanationEn: Niet mogen expresses prohibition: je mag hier niet roken.

exercises.prompt: Wij ___ graag een kopje koffie. (would like)
exercises.explanationEn: Willen expresses wanting; for a polite order, we willen graag... is common.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: With a modal verb, the second verb stays in the infinitive at the end.

exercises.prompt: Match the modal verb to its common meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: Meanings vary slightly with context; these are common A2 uses.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: If a time phrase starts the sentence, the finite verb comes second and the subject follows it.
acceptedSentences: Morgen ga ik met de bus naar mijn werk.

exercises.prompt: Vandaag ___ ik thuis. (werken)
exercises.explanationEn: The verb is in second position; with ik, use the stem werk.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: After omdat, the conjugated verb goes to the end of the subordinate clause.
acceptedSentences: Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence part to its role.
exercises.explanationEn: Recognizing sentence parts helps with Dutch word order.

exercises.prompt: Morgen ___ we naar de markt. (gaan)
exercises.explanationEn: When a time expression comes first, the finite verb comes before the subject: Morgen gaan we...

exercises.prompt: Na het werk ___ ik boodschappen. (doen, present)
exercises.explanationEn: After a fronted phrase, inversion puts the verb before ik: Na het werk doe ik...

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: The sentence starts with daarna, so the verb belt comes before the subject zij.

exercises.prompt: Match the first phrase to the correct continuation.
exercises.explanationEn: A time/place phrase at the start is followed by the finite verb, then the subject.

exercises.prompt: Ik heb gisteren een brief ___. (schrijven)
exercises.explanationEn: Perfectum = hebben/zijn + past participle; schrijven → geschreven.

exercises.prompt: Zij is naar huis ___. (gaan)
exercises.explanationEn: Use is + gegaan for the perfectum of gaan.

exercises.prompt: We hebben de film ___. (zien)
exercises.explanationEn: Zien has the irregular past participle gezien.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: The auxiliary comes in second position and the participle usually goes at the end.

exercises.prompt: Match the infinitive to the past participle.
exercises.explanationEn: Irregular participles often need to be learned individually.

exercises.prompt: Ik ___ de televisie ___. (uitzetten, present)
exercises.explanationEn: In a main clause, the conjugated verb comes second and the separable prefix goes to the end: Ik zet de televisie uit.

exercises.prompt: Morgen ___ ik mijn moeder ___. (opbellen, present)
exercises.explanationEn: With inversion, the finite verb still stays in second position; the prefix goes to the end.

exercises.prompt: Ik heb de deur ___. (opendoen, perfectum)
exercises.explanationEn: In the perfectum, the prefix is joined to the participle: opengedaan.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: In a main clause, opruimen separates: ruim ... op.
acceptedSentences: Ik ruim mijn kamer morgen op.

exercises.prompt: Match the separable verb to its meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: The prefix often moves to the end in a main clause.

exercises.prompt: Ik blijf thuis, ___ ik ziek ben. (because)
exercises.explanationEn: Omdat means because and introduces a subordinate clause: ... omdat ik ziek ben.

exercises.prompt: Ik wil fietsen, ___ het regent. (but)
exercises.explanationEn: Maar means but and connects contrasting ideas.

exercises.prompt: Ik neem een jas mee, ___ het koud is. (because)
exercises.explanationEn: Want means because; unlike omdat, it keeps normal main-clause word order.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: After omdat, the verb goes to the end of the subordinate clause.
acceptedSentences: Ik ga naar bed omdat ik moe ben.

exercises.prompt: Match the conjunction to its meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: Pay special attention to the word order after want versus omdat.

exercises.prompt: Eén boek, twee ___.
exercises.explanationEn: Many Dutch nouns form the plural with -en; spelling may change.

exercises.prompt: Eén tafel, drie ___.
exercises.explanationEn: Many nouns form the plural with -s when the ending allows it.

exercises.prompt: Eén kind, twee ___.
exercises.explanationEn: Kind has the irregular plural kinderen.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: Plural subject de kinderen takes the plural verb spelen.

exercises.prompt: Match the singular noun to its plural.
exercises.explanationEn: Some plurals change spelling or vowel; learn common forms.

exercises.prompt: Mijn huis is ___ dan jouw huis. (small)
exercises.explanationEn: Comparative usually adds -er: klein → kleiner; use dan for 'than'.

exercises.prompt: Dit is de ___ supermarkt in de buurt. (cheap)
exercises.explanationEn: The superlative commonly uses -st(e) and often de/het before the noun.

exercises.prompt: De trein is ___ dan de bus. (fast)
exercises.explanationEn: Use the comparative sneller with dan.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: The comparative adjective comes before dan.
acceptedSentences: Deze tas is duurder dan die tas.

exercises.prompt: Match the adjective to its comparative.
exercises.explanationEn: Goed → beter is irregular; veel → meer and weinig → minder are also irregular.

exercises.prompt: Ik heb ___ tijd. (no / not any)
exercises.explanationEn: Use geen before an indefinite noun: geen tijd.

exercises.prompt: Ik begrijp het ___. (not)
exercises.explanationEn: Use niet to negate a verb, adjective, or definite expression: ik begrijp het niet.

exercises.prompt: Ik drink ___ koffie. (never)
exercises.explanationEn: Nooit means never.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: Niet often appears before the phrase being negated or toward the end of the clause.
acceptedSentences: Ik ga vandaag niet met de auto.

exercises.prompt: Match the negative word to its meaning.
exercises.explanationEn: Choose the negative form based on what is being negated.

exercises.prompt: ___ boek is van mij. (this; het-word)
exercises.explanationEn: Use dit with singular het-words nearby: dit boek.

exercises.prompt: ___ fiets is nieuw. (that; de-word)
exercises.explanationEn: Use die for a de-word farther away: die fiets.

exercises.prompt: ___ huizen zijn duur. (these)
exercises.explanationEn: Use deze with plural nouns for 'these'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: Demonstratives come before the noun: dat huis, dit huis.
acceptedSentences: Dat huis is groter dan dit huis.

exercises.prompt: Match the demonstrative to its use.
exercises.explanationEn: For singular nouns, first identify whether the noun uses de or het.

exercises.prompt: Omdat het regent, ___ ik thuis. (blijven)
exercises.explanationEn: The subordinate clause comes first; the main clause then uses inversion: blijf ik.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order.
exercises.explanationEn: Time first → inversion; perfectum participle at the end.
acceptedSentences: Gisteren heb ik mijn boodschappen gedaan.

exercises.prompt: Mijn ouders ___ gisteren vroeg naar huis gegaan.
exercises.explanationEn: Zijn is used with gaan in the perfectum.

exercises.prompt: Match the sentence to the grammar point.
exercises.explanationEn: Mixed review connects individual rules to realistic A2 sentences.
